## db7f22490768

**Reproduced defect — dishonest/dead control contract.** Generator SHA-256 `84860927b976d04eef2c979e8e017eead8d101f509934edbf95109b93cc55505` advertises `palette_kind`, `palette_size`, `position_bias`, `n_distinct_colors`, and `density`, but generation reads none of them. At seed 123, sample index 7, medium difficulty, `palette_kind=warm`, `palette_kind=cool`, `palette_size=1`, `n_distinct_colors=1`, `position_bias=scattered_hollow_rects`, and `density=sparse` were all accepted, validator-clean, and byte-identical to the default grid. An unknown `unknown_axis=99` was also accepted and identical.

The reproducible report is `checks/audit/db7f22490768/override_reproducer.json`; `checks/audit/run_local_probes.py` rebuilds it. I additionally sampled 200 inputs per band (600 total): all were distinct within their band and had zero validator errors, so the finding is not a crash/degeneracy artifact. It means curriculum requests can be silently ignored and the advertised palette families do not create observable variation. No fix was made, as required for an audit target.

The generic override stage was also attempted and exceeded the external 300-second execution window, leaving an honestly incomplete running receipt under `checks/audit/db7f22490768-override/`; it is not cited as a pass or failure.
